content.user_title: Manage Lark Drive Files and Permissions
content.value_statement: Lark Drive work often requires many commands and careful token handling. This skill guides safe file, folder, comment, version, and permission workflows through lark-cli.
actual_capabilities: Search Lark Drive and Wiki resources by title, owner, type, and activity filters.
Upload, download, import, export, preview, and inspect supported Drive resources.
Create folders, copy resources, move items, and build shortcuts with token-aware routing.
Manage comments, reactions, permission requests, collaborators, public settings, security labels, and ownership workflows.
Compare, pull, push, and synchronize local files with Drive folders using documented conflict controls.
List, download, revert, and delete supported file versions.
limitations: Requires installed lark-cli and valid Lark or Feishu authentication, scopes, and resource access.
Does not edit document bodies, spreadsheet cells, Base records, or Wiki hierarchy content.
Some operations depend on tenant rollout, document type, identity mode, API limits, and organization policy.
Destructive and permission-changing operations require explicit confirmation and may not provide complete rollback.

use_cases.title: Organize a shared Drive
use_cases.description: Inventory folders, identify duplicates or temporary content, and prepare a confirmed organization plan.

use_cases.title: Review access exposure
use_cases.description: Assess public links, external access, security labels, and ownership before proposing permission changes.

use_cases.title: Synchronize project files
use_cases.description: Compare local files with Drive, resolve conflicts, and transfer approved changes with clear results.

prompt_templates.title: List a folder
prompt_templates.prompt: List the files in this Lark Drive folder: [URL]. Show names, types, paths, and access errors. Do not modify anything.

prompt_templates.title: Upload a file
prompt_templates.prompt: Upload [local file] to [folder URL]. Inspect the target first, use the correct token type, and ask before any overwrite.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a synchronization
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [local directory] with [Drive folder URL]. Report new, modified, and conflicting files. Propose a synchronization plan without changing either side.

prompt_templates.title: Audit permissions
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit permissions for [scope]. Identify public links, external access, ownership concerns, and missing evidence. Produce a remediation plan, then wait for confirmation.

output_examples.input: Find files I edited this week containing quarterly plan.
output: Found six matching resources across Drive and Wiki.
The top result is Quarterly Plan, edited yesterday and owned by Finance.
Two resources were excluded because access was denied.

output_examples.input: Check whether this document is publicly accessible.
output: The document allows company-wide link viewing.
External access is closed, and public internet access was not found.
Collaborator membership and audit history were outside this check.

output_examples.input: Compare my local release folder with the Drive release folder.
output: Three local files are new, one remote file is newer, and two files match.
Review the newer remote file before selecting a synchronization policy.

best_practices: Inspect URLs and tokens before selecting a command or resource type.
Use read-only checks and dry runs before uploads, moves, permission changes, or synchronization.
Confirm exact targets, identities, scopes, and conflict policies before high-impact operations.
anti_patterns: Do not treat Wiki node tokens as Drive file tokens without inspection.
Do not bypass confirmation for deletes, ownership transfers, broad permission changes, or remote cleanup.
Do not use this skill for document body editing, spreadsheet cells, Base records, or Wiki hierarchy changes.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages Lark Drive resources, transfers, comments, versions, synchronization, and selected permission workflows.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Install lark-cli, authenticate a supported Lark or Feishu identity, and grant the scopes required by each operation.

faq.question: Can it edit document content?
faq.answer: No. Use the dedicated document, spreadsheet, Base, Wiki, or Markdown skill for content-level changes.

faq.question: How are destructive actions protected?
faq.answer: The guidance uses explicit confirmation, dry runs, scope checks, target review, and verification where supported.

faq.question: Does it support Feishu and Doubao resource links?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes supported resource URLs by path and token type instead of using generic web retrieval.

faq.question: Can it synchronize any local directory?
faq.answer: No. Local paths must remain inside the working directory, and synchronization supports documented Drive file types and conflict policies.
